test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They __are looking to__ a place to rest.
solution:
The correct answer is "**are looking for"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The meaning of the sentence is that they are searching for a place to take a rest.
 
• The underlined words of the given sentence are **"are looking to"** . The phrase **"looking to"** means someone is planning to do something.
 
• Here we need to put the verb which refers to search a place to take a rest. The term **"look for"** would be used to describe looking for a specific item; the object is to locate the item.
 
• According to the meaning of the sentence,** "are looking for"** is the correct answer in replaces of **"are looking to"**. "Are looking for" means **"searching for something"**.

So the correct sentence will be **They are looking for__ a place to rest.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look into the other words.
 
• The first option intends to give a look with attention. We can refer to a sentence as an example.
 
 
• ***Example:** I decided to have a **look at** that book.*
 
 
 
• We can use **"should be looking" **which means something which is our duty to give a look. 
 
 
• ***Example: **We **should be looking** at the tiger.*
 
 
 
• "Look into" means to research something intricate in order to comprehend its complexities better; a better comprehension is the end result.
 
 
• ***Example: **We **are looking into** this matter.*
